title: Releasing hoop tension without distorting the work
subtitle: How and when to remove fabric from a hoop to prevent permanent ring marks and fibre stress.
excerpt: Fabric left in a hoop at the end of a session picks up ring marks and stress that become permanent. Releasing tension correctly at the end of each session and re-mounting fresh at the start of the next one keeps the cloth in good condition.
sourceNotes:
Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), Project Gutenberg #20776. Care of fabric and hoop practice.
Weldon's Practical Needlework, volume 1 (1886), Internet Archive. Fabric care in hoop work.

glossaryTerms.definition: A circular impression left on fabric after a wooden hoop has been left mounted for an extended period. Can be permanent on linen and fine evenweave if not removed promptly.

content.text: Fabric left in a wooden hoop overnight, or longer, risks a

: a faint indented circle that sets in the fibres. On linen and fine evenweave the mark can be permanent. Removing the fabric at the end of every session takes ten seconds and prevents the problem entirely.
How to release the hoop safely
At the end of a stitching session, park the needle safely in the border of the cloth or on a needle minder.
Loosen the screw on the outer ring until the two rings separate without resistance.
Lift the outer ring off the fabric. Do not twist it; lift straight up.
Slide the inner ring out from beneath the fabric. The cloth is now free.
If a ring mark is visible, dampen the area lightly with a clean damp cloth and smooth the fibres back into place while the fabric is flat. Allow to dry flat.
Store the cloth rolled or flat, not folded through the design area.

attrs.heading: What goes wrong
attrs.intro: Hoop tension problems and their solutions.

items.symptom: Ring mark won't come out despite dampening
items.cause: The fabric was left in the hoop for several days or weeks, and the fibres have set.
items.fix: Wash the whole piece gently in cool water, smooth flat, and dry under a light weight. Pressing through a damp cloth once fully dry may help on cotton. On linen, the mark may be permanent.

items.symptom: The stitches look distorted when the hoop is removed
items.cause: The fabric was under too much tension in the hoop, pulling the weave out of square.
items.fix: Re-mount with less tension, keeping the grain square. The stitches usually relax back once the cloth is released.

content.text: Releasing tension at the end of each session is a habit that protects all needlework cloth. The
routine applies to all hoop sizes and is especially important for linen and fine evenweave that cannot be easily washed to remove marks.
